# Sharkbite → Shoal compatibility matrix

Exhaustive enumeration of the public Sharkbite compatibility contract and its
mapping onto Shoal. This document is the coverage gate for
[phrocker/sharkbite#108](https://github.com/phrocker/sharkbite/issues/108) and
Shoal issue [#81](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/81) (umbrella
[#59](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/59)).

## 2. Release gate (normative)

This gate is the deliverable of Shoal issue
[#81](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/81); that issue is where
gate status, the independent omission/classification audit, and any approval
decisions are recorded. Closing #81 requires this document plus that audit —
not the document alone.

There are **two** gates, and conflating them is what made revision 1's single
gate circular: no row can reach `Covered` until code exists, so a gate that
demands universal `Covered` before any work starts would forbid the work that
satisfies it.

### 2.1 Implementation-entry gate

Work on a Sharkbite-compatible Python layer may begin when, for the rows it
touches:

1. The row is enumerated here with its Sharkbite signature, defaults, and
   layer mapping — that is, the contract is known before it is implemented.
2. Its prerequisite stage is met ([§23](#sec-23)): Go parity before C ABI
   parity, C ABI parity before compatibility tests, tests before wheels.
3. Any divergence it depends on is either approved in [§26](#sec-26) or
   explicitly recorded as an open question with a named owner.

This gate is per-row and forward-looking. It permits prototyping, spikes, and
merged implementation work behind a feature flag. It does **not** permit
publishing, naming, or describing anything as Sharkbite-compatible.

### 2.2 Final release gate

> **Gate.** No release, no publication under the name `sharkbite`, and no
> "Sharkbite compatible" claim until **every required row** in [§5](#sec-5)
> through [§20](#sec-20) is either `Covered` with at least one **named**
> automated test on each layer it claims (Go and, where applicable, C ABI), or
> is recorded as `Intentional divergence` **and** has recorded explicit human
> approval in [§26](#sec-26).

**Required rows** are selected by the normative
[client-scope ADR](sharkbite-client-scope.md) and pinned, in matrix order, in
`docs/sharkbite-compatibility-revision56-scope.tsv`. Historical C++ headers and
tests, the dead embedded module, and Torch/pandas extras remain audited but are
`Optional`; scope never changes their underlying implementation status. Core
Python/client rows stay required unless individually justified as
`Not required`. As of revision 56, **394 rows are required, 390 are satisfied,
and 4 remain**. The satisfied set is 292 required rows whose matrix status is
`Covered` plus 98 approved divergences. The remaining required gaps are 1
`Missing Go` and 3 `Behavior mismatch` rows.

`SB-XCUT-014`, `SB-XCUT-019`, and `SB-PKG-008` remain explicit
optional/deferred macOS-native environment/runtime gaps under @phrocker's
2026-08-20 owner decision; their detailed statuses still record missing native
evidence. `SB-PKG-011` is covered by the controlled Linux manylinux workflow
and verified main-branch run; macOS publication remains optional. Live
Accumulo conformance remains external evidence under #74 and does not convert
an uncovered row into coverage.

Corollaries, all binding:

1. **No hidden core gaps.** The package may omit surfaces classified
   `Optional`, but every required importable or documented Python API must be
   present, explicitly approved as a divergence, or reported as a blocker.
   Optional C++ source compatibility must not be implied by the Python
   compatibility claim.
2. **No name-based coverage claims.** A row may only be marked `Covered` when
   the Shoal symbol has been read and its semantics compared against the
   Sharkbite behavior. Matching identifiers (`Scanner`, `Mutation`, `flush`,
   `close`) are not evidence.
3. **Ordered prerequisites.** Work proceeds strictly in the order
   Go parity → C ABI parity → compatibility tests → Python/wheels
   ([§23](#sec-23)). A row cannot advance past a layer whose predecessor is
   unmet.
4. **Named tests only.** "Covered by the existing suite" is not evidence. Each
   `Covered` row names test functions or C assertion blocks.
5. **Divergence requires approval.** `Intentional divergence` rows are
   proposals until a named approver signs [§26](#sec-26). Unapproved
   divergences block the gate exactly like `Missing Go`.
6. **Live-cluster conformance is part of the gate.** Unit tests alone cannot
   close rows whose semantics are defined by a real tablet server
   ([§24](#sec-24)).

### 3.2 Shoal inputs actually inspected

`table_bulk_import.go` is new since the previous pin),
`accumulo/*_test.go` (14 files, 94 `func Test…(t *testing.T)` functions,
names extracted mechanically),
`capi/include/shoal.h`, `capi/include/shoal_types.h`, `capi/README.md`,
`capi/tests/{lifecycle.c,result_bridge.c,header_cpp_test.cpp,test_seam.h}`,
`cmd/shoal-capi/*.go`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,

and the `internal/` packages named in matrix rows.

### 3.3 Evidence-validation method

Every Shoal symbol, path, and test name cited below was validated against the
`origin/main` worktree, not against memory or a prior summary:

1. **Path existence** — each cited file was confirmed present with
   `Test-Path` or a direct read.
2. **Symbol existence** — exported Go declarations were extracted mechanically
   (`^(func|type|const|var)` over `accumulo/*.go`) and cross-checked against
   file/line before citation. C ABI declarations were extracted from
   `capi/include/shoal.h` and `capi/include/shoal_types.h` by full read.
3. **Test names** — extracted mechanically (`^func Test`) from
   `accumulo/*_test.go` and `cmd/shoal-capi/*_test.go`; C assertion blocks were
   read from `capi/tests/*.c` and cited by stable function/file anchors rather
   than mutable local line numbers wherever the matrix format permits.
4. **Absence claims** — every "absent" claim was produced by a negative search
   (for example, no `Namespace`, `Permission`, `GrantAuthorizations`,
   `AddSplits`, `ListSplits`, `Compact`, `ImportTable`, `ExportTable`,
   `CloneTable`, `Online`/`Offline`, `Merge`, or `DeleteRows` symbol exists in
   `accumulo/`), not by omission from a summary.
5. **C++ inventory** — the complete public-declaration inventory in
   [§19](#sec-19) is produced by a semantic scanner over every header, and the
   resulting rows are checked back against that inventory by the ten-check
   verifier in [§19.3](#sec-19-3): row count identity, orphan citation,
   unenumerated declaration, parser artifact, scope leak, empty enum, hidden
   duplicate, malformed row, callable misclassification, and silent drop.
6. **Sharkbite claims** — validated against the pinned clone. Where an
   intermediate summary disagreed with the source (for example a claimed
   three-argument `Range(start, end, bool)` call in
   `examples/pythonexample.py`), the source won: that file uses the four-argument
   form at `examples/pythonexample.py:92`.

**Delivery status.** PR [#92](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/pull/92) has

The correction is not cosmetic: on the merged text a reader would conclude that

## 4. How to read the matrix

### 4.1 Columns

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ID | Stable row anchor. Never renumber; retire with a tombstone instead. |
| Sharkbite | Python-visible symbol (or C++ symbol for [§19](#sec-19)) with its pinned signature/defaults. |
| Shoal Go | Exact Go symbol in `accumulo/` (or an internal package, marked as such) or `—` when absent. |
| Shoal C ABI | Exact declaration in `capi/include/shoal.h` / `shoal_types.h`, or `—` when absent. |
| Evidence | Named tests, on both layers where both are claimed. `—` means no test exists. |
| Status | One of the six values below. |
| Notes | Semantics, defaults, ownership, and shim requirements. |

### 4.2 Status decision procedure

Applied top-down; the first matching rule wins.

1. **`Missing Go`** — no Go implementation exists in `accumulo/` or a reachable
   internal package. This is the bottom-most gap and always blocks first.
2. **`Missing C ABI`** — a Go implementation exists but the capability is not
   reachable through `capi/include/shoal.h`. This bucket also covers rows whose
   only remaining work is above the ABI (wheels, packaging, Python shims),
   because such rows are still unreachable from Python today.
3. **`Behavior mismatch`** — reachable on both layers, but user-visible
   semantics differ (types, defaults, ordering, lifetime, error class,
   binary handling, streaming vs materialized).
4. **`Intentional divergence (approval required)`** — deliberately not
   reproduced; requires a signed entry in [§26](#sec-26).
5. **`Not required (rationale required)`** — out of the compatibility contract;
   requires a stated rationale in the Notes column.
6. **`Covered`** — reachable with equivalent semantics on every layer the row
   claims, with named tests on each of those layers.

A row only owes evidence for the layers its `Shoal Go` and `Shoal C ABI`
columns actually name. Where a column reads `n/a`, `implicit`, or `—`, no
separate test is owed for that layer, and the row must say why in Notes.
`cmd/shoal-capi/*_test.go` counts as C ABI evidence: those tests exercise the
exported ABI entry points directly, and `TestSharedLibraryCABI`
(`cmd/shoal-capi/cabi_test.go`) is the harness that builds the `c-shared`
library and compiles, links, and runs `main()` in `capi/tests/lifecycle.c` and
`main()` in `capi/tests/result_bridge.c` against it.

**Unproven equivalence counts as difference.** A capability that is reachable
on both layers but whose Sharkbite-visible semantics are not demonstrated by a
named test is recorded as `Behavior mismatch`, not `Covered`, and its Notes
must name the test that would close it. Tests that only prove argument
validation, struct sizing, handle lifecycle, or construction do **not** prove
the semantics of the operation they configure, and a test that links against
internal implementation files rather than the exported library does not prove
anything about the ABI. Two independent audits have now applied this rule: the
first reclassified 26 rows (marked `audit #92` in Notes), the second a further
11 (marked `audit #2`).

### 4.3 Layer legend

`Go` = `accumulo/` package. `ABI` = `capi/include/shoal.h`.
`internal` = present in Shoal but not exported (`internal/...`); an internal
implementation never satisfies a row on its own, because Sharkbite consumers
cannot reach it — it only shortens the Go-parity work.

states "package import is now **sharkbite** not **pysharkbite**", while
`sharkbite/__init__.py:5` re-exports the native module, so **both** names are
importable and both are used by the pinned tests and examples.

| SB-CFG-035 | `virtual ZookeeperInstance::getServers()` returning `vector<shared_ptr<ServerConnection>>` (`include/data/constructs/client/zookeeperinstance.h:222`) | `Instance.Servers(ctx)` (`accumulo/instance.go:52`), `zkLocator.Servers` (`accumulo/topology.go:149`), `ServerConnection` (`accumulo/topology.go:34`), `ClientServices` (`internal/zk/manager.go:327`) | `shoal_connector_get_servers`, `shoal_server_list_get` (`capi/include/shoal.h`) | `TestInstanceRootTabletLocation`, `TestInstanceManagerLocations`, `TestInstanceServers`, `TestInstanceZooKeepersRootAndConfiguration`, `TestStaticInstanceTopology`, `TestInstanceTopologyCancelsInFlightReads`, `TestInstanceTopologyAfterCloseRejectsLiveDiscovery` (`accumulo/topology_test.go`); `TestClientServicesReportsKindGroupAndOrder`, `TestClientServicesOrdersByServerIdentity`, `TestClientServicesPromotesNextSurvivingServerLock`, `TestClientServicesUsesOnlyTheSurvivingHolderLock` (`internal/zk/topology_test.go`); `main()` (`capi/tests/lifecycle.c`) | Covered | **Accumulo 4 wire divergence, richer result.** Sharkbite reads the flat 1.x `<root>/tservers` layout; Accumulo 4 publishes lock znodes under `/accumulo/<id>/{tservers,sservers,compactors}/<resource-group>/<server>`, so every endpoint carries `Kind` and `Group` in addition to host and port. <a id="sec-9"></a>

## 9. Matrix: scanners and result iteration (`SB-SCAN`)

Sharkbite exposes exactly one scanner type to Python — `scanners::BatchScanner`
bound as `BatchScanner` (`pysharkbite.cpp:434`) — returned by
`AccumuloTableOperations.createScanner(auths, threads)`, which calls
`createSharedScanner` (`include/interconnect/python/PythonStructures.h:172-175`).

### 9.2 PyTorch dataset surface (`SB-TORCH`)

`sharkbite/torch.py` is shipped inside the `sharkbite` distribution
(`setup.py:50` packages `sharkbite`, which contains `torch.py`), so
`import sharkbite.torch` is part of the published import contract. Every row is
`Missing C ABI`: the surface is pure Python over a scanner, so it unblocks only
after scanning is reachable from Python, and two of its members are defective
today ([SB-UNSAFE-021](#sec-21), [SB-UNSAFE-022](#sec-21)).

| ID | Sharkbite | Shoal Go | Shoal C ABI | Evidence | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SB-TORCH-001 | `sharkbite.torch` module import, requiring `torch.utils.data` at import time (`sharkbite/torch.py:1`) | — | — | `examples/torchexample.py` | Missing C ABI | Importing `sharkbite.torch` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` when PyTorch is absent; the shim must keep it an optional extra with the same module path. |
| SB-TORCH-002 | `AccumuloCluster(instance, zookeepers, username, password, table=None, auths=None)`, subclassing `AccumuloBase` and `IterableDataset` (`sharkbite/torch.py:5-7`) | — | — | — | Missing C ABI | Adds no behavior over `AccumuloBase`; the value is the `IterableDataset` base class, which PyTorch's `DataLoader` type-checks. |
| SB-TORCH-003 | `AccumuloDataset(instance, zookeepers, username, password, table, auths, start_key_string, end_key_string, user_lambda=None)` (`sharkbite/torch.py:14-22`) | — | — | `examples/torchexample.py` | Missing C ABI | Constructor side effects are contractual: it builds `Range(start, True, end, False)`, calls `createScanner(auths, self._threads)`, and calls `addRange` immediately, so the scan range is fixed at construction and `_threads` is captured then ([SB-UNSAFE-023](#sec-21)). |
| SB-TORCH-004 | `AccumuloDataset.coerce(key)` (`sharkbite/torch.py:24-36`) | — | — | `examples/torchexample.py` | Missing C ABI | Two paths: with `user_lambda`, call it on the `KeyValue`; without, attempt an `int(...)` conversion. Both swallow every exception and return `0`. Defective — see [SB-UNSAFE-021](#sec-21). |
| SB-TORCH-005 | `AccumuloDataset.__iter__` (`sharkbite/torch.py:56-62`) | — | — | `examples/torchexample.py` | Missing C ABI | Lazily calls `getResultSet()` once and caches both the result set and its iterator, so a second `iter()` on the same dataset resumes rather than restarts — the opposite of `Results.__iter__` ([SB-SCAN-017](#sec-9)). |
| SB-TORCH-006 | `AccumuloDataset.__next__` (`sharkbite/torch.py:38-54`) | — | — | `examples/torchexample.py` | Missing C ABI | Raises `StopIteration` when never iterated; on exhaustion it closes the underlying scanner and clears its cached iterators, so the dataset cannot be re-iterated after one pass. A `coerce` result of `None` also terminates iteration. |
| SB-TORCH-007 | `AccumuloValueDataset(cluster, table, start_key_string, end_key_string)` (`sharkbite/torch.py:64-66`) | — | — | — | Missing C ABI | Constructor is broken in the pinned release ([SB-UNSAFE-022](#sec-21)); the intended contract is an `AccumuloDataset` whose `coerce` returns the cell value. |
| SB-TORCH-008 | `AccumuloValueDataset.coerce(key)` returning `key.getValue().get()` (`sharkbite/torch.py:68-69`) | — | — | — | Missing C ABI | Returns a decoded `str`, so it inherits the binary-safety defect of `Value.get()` ([SB-UNSAFE-002](#sec-21)). |
| SB-TORCH-009 | `torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset, num_workers=0)` compatibility (`examples/torchexample.py`) | — | — | `examples/torchexample.py` | Missing C ABI | The datasets must remain usable as `IterableDataset`s; `num_workers > 0` forks worker processes, which interacts with [SB-XCUT-018](#sec-20) fork safety. |

### 9.3 pandas surface (`SB-PANDA`)

Enumerated because `pandashark` consumes the high-level `sharkbite` API
directly ([SB-PKG-013](#sec-5)). Every row is `Missing C ABI`.

Because `AccumuloIterator.__iter__` calls `Results.__iter__`, which **restarts** the server-side scan ([SB-SCAN-017](#sec-9)), re-iterating a `DataFrameIterator` silently re-reads from the beginning. |

## 10. Matrix: writers (`SB-WRITE`)

Sharkbite's Python `BatchWriter` is `writer::Sink<KeyValue>`
(`pysharkbite.cpp:486`), created by
`tableOps.createWriter(auths, threads)` → `createSharedWriter`
(`include/interconnect/python/PythonStructures.h:177-180`).

| ID | Sharkbite | Shoal Go | Shoal C ABI | Evidence | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### 10.1 High-level Python helper classes (`SB-BASE`)

`sharkbite/__init__.py` is shipped by the `sharkbite` distribution
(`setup.py:50`) and star-exports the native module, so these classes are part of
the published API even though they are pure Python. Every row is
`Missing C ABI`: each is composable from the Go client, but nothing above the C
ABI exists yet.

Installing a class the table already carries returns its existing number without writing, because a second number would run the same check twice per mutation. Allocation is a compare-and-set: the table's own properties are read with their version and written back through `modifyTableProperties`, so a second client that installs a constraint first makes the losing write fail with a concurrent modification, which is retried against the winner's state rather than overwriting it. **Safe shim for unsafe C++ behavior:** the pinned `addConstraint` is a stub that installs nothing and returns 0 ([SB-UNSAFE-036](#sec-21)), so no Sharkbite program has a working constraint to preserve. Listing and removal have no Sharkbite equivalent but are required to make the returned number usable. Revision 29 exposes the owned, deadline-aware ABI with connector-close coordination and allocation-failure coverage. |

<a id="sec-14"></a>

## 14. Matrix: cluster status and monitoring (`SB-STAT`)

Reached through `AccumuloConnector.getStatistics()` (`pysharkbite.cpp:268`) and
demonstrated by `examples/pythonstats.py`.

**All 82 capability rows in this section are
`Intentional divergence (approval required)` because the upstream capability no
longer exists.** Two rows are excluded and carry other statuses:
[SB-STAT-028](#sec-14) (`Not required` — a pybind11 registration defect in the
`TableRates` property table, not a capability) and [SB-STAT-038](#sec-14)
(`Covered` — the Python status placeholder types preserve `dynamic_attr` through
normal instance dictionaries). Accumulo commit `f0841e4` removed
`getManagerStats`, `ManagerMonitorInfo`, and `DeadServer` together with the
legacy monitor resources — 113 commits before the pinned Accumulo 4 target
`317c288`. The surviving REST-v2, metrics, and server APIs cannot reconstruct
the legacy status object graph.

The status label keeps the words `approval required` because [§4.2](#sec-4)
fixes the six status names; approval state lives in [§26](#sec-26). The entry
point [SB-CONN-007](#sec-7) is not one of the 82 approved rows, but is now
`Covered`: the buildable Python shim required by the decision has landed and is
tested. That classification proves the raising entry point, not cluster-status
support. The single approval decision governing them is
[SB-DIV-016](#sec-26), and it covers the 82 capability rows of this section —
neither [SB-STAT-028](#sec-14) nor [SB-STAT-038](#sec-14) is in it.

**Approved — @phrocker, 2026-08-19.** The decision is recorded on Shoal issue
[#81](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/81#issuecomment-5343583850)
and mirrored here by revision 40. The approved compatibility behavior is
normative:

1. `connector.getStatistics()` **raises `NotImplementedError`** with a stable
   explanation that Accumulo 4 removed the legacy manager-monitor API.
2. It **must not** return a fabricated or partially populated status object.
3. This permanent absence **must not** be surfaced as a retryable
   `ClientException`.
4. **Capability discovery must not advertise cluster-status support.**

Revision 54 proves these obligations with
`test_connector_statistics_and_closed_lifecycle_are_stable` and
`test_status_placeholders_preserve_dynamic_attributes`
(`python/tests/test_foundation.py`). No status object is returned, the exception
is stable and non-retryable, no cluster-status capability is advertised, and
all eight importable placeholder types accept arbitrary user attributes.
**each of the 82 rows [SB-DIV-016](#sec-26) covers keeps `Intentional divergence
(approval required)` permanently**; only the separately buildable entry point
and dynamic-attribute row moved to `Covered`.

<a id="sec-15"></a>

## 15. Matrix: RFile, iterators, and streams (`SB-RFILE`)

Shoal now publishes an `rfile` package that is the Go form of this section's
surface: `Create` (`rfile/writer.go:50`) writes a file, `Open`
(`rfile/reader.go:70`) and `OpenSequential` (`rfile/reader.go:81`) read one,
`OpenMany` (`rfile/reader.go:145`) merges several, `KeyValueIterator`
(`rfile/reader.go:28`) is the cursor contract they all satisfy, and `Seekable`
(`rfile/seekable.go:28`) is the relocation every read takes. Keys and values
cross the boundary as copies, every operation takes a context, and the package
documents its lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency, and binary-data behavior.
The writer now finalizes the current group and starts a named independently
sorted stream when `AddLocalityGroup` is called.

| ID | Sharkbite | Shoal Go | Shoal C ABI | Evidence | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SB-RFILE-001 | `RFileOperations.openForWrite(path) -> SequentialRFile` (`pysharkbite.cpp:589`, `include/data/constructs/rfile/RFileOperations.h:43`) | `Create(ctx, path string, opts WriterOptions) (*Writer, error)` (`rfile/writer.go:50`) | `shoal_rfile_writer_create`, `shoal_rfile_writer_free` | `TestWriteThenReadSequentially`, `TestWriterRejectsOutOfOrderAppendAndUseAfterClose`, `TestWriterCopiesTheCallersBuffers`, `TestCreateRejectsAnUnsupportedCodecWithoutTouchingTheFile` (`rfile/rfile_test.go`); `test/python/TestRFileWrites.py:35-43`; linked C11/C++11 `TestSharedLibraryCABI`; `TestRFileLifecycleCloseCancelsAndWaits`, `TestRFileLifecycleConcurrentRetainAndClose`, `TestRFileLifecycleDeadline` (`cmd/shoal-capi/rfile_export_test.go`) | Covered | The public `rfile` package now exports Shoal's writer. `Create` validates the options first, so an unregistered codec is `ErrUnsupportedCodec` (`rfile/errors.go:24`) before anything is opened; it then creates or truncates the path and the bytes on disk are a valid RFile only once `Writer.Close` (`rfile/writer.go:145`) returns without error, which is the same two-step contract as `openForWrite` plus `close`. No ABI entry point exports it yet. |

A missing or range-less relocation is `ErrInvalidSeekable` (`rfile/errors.go:17`) rather than a null dereference, and seeking is repeatable: the reader may be repositioned any number of times. Row bounds are resolved to absolute key bounds through `Range.KeyBounds` (`accumulo/range.go:143`), so an exclusive start row skips the whole row and an inclusive end row keeps all of it. The boundary is the *first possible key* of the row, carrying the maximum timestamp because Accumulo sorts timestamps descending: a cell with an empty column family and a positive timestamp sorts before `Key{Row: R, Timestamp: 0}` and would otherwise fall on the wrong side of both bounds. |

It closes every file the reader opened, including all inputs of [SB-RFILE-004](#sec-15), a failed open closes the handles it had already taken, and a failed close is remembered so a later call cannot report success. |
| SB-RFILE-011 | `SequentialRFile.append(KeyValue) -> bool` (`pysharkbite.cpp:530`) | `Writer.Append(ctx, entry Entry) error` (`rfile/writer.go:87`) | `shoal_rfile_writer_append`, `shoal_rfile_entry` | `TestWriteThenReadSequentially`, `TestWriterRejectsOutOfOrderAppendAndUseAfterClose`, `TestWriterCopiesTheCallersBuffers`, `TestBinaryDataRoundTrips`, `TestTombstonesRoundTrip`, `TestTombstoneAndLiveEntryAtOneTimestampAppendInOrder` (`rfile/rfile_test.go`); `TestFailedAppendIsTerminal` (`rfile/close_internal_test.go`); `test/python/TestRFileWrites.py:41`; linked C11/C++11 `TestSharedLibraryCABI`; `TestRFileLifecycleCloseCancelsAndWaits`, `TestRFileLifecycleConcurrentRetainAndClose`, `TestRFileLifecycleDeadline` (`cmd/shoal-capi/rfile_export_test.go`) | Covered | **Safe shim for unsafe C++ behavior:** Sharkbite returns `bool` and never checks ordering ([SB-UNSAFE-033](#sec-21)), so an out-of-order append silently writes a malformed RFile; Go rejects it with `ErrOutOfOrder` (`rfile/errors.go:28`) before any byte is written. Appending after `Close` is `ErrClosed`, matching the `std::runtime_error` Sharkbite throws. Ordering uses Accumulo's full comparison including the deleted bit, so a tombstone and the live entry at one coordinate and timestamp append in that order. A failed append is terminal, because the entry has already reached the block stream: the error is latched, later appends return it, and `Close` reports it even when finalization succeeds, so a partial file is never committed as complete. The key and value are copied, so the caller may reuse its buffers, and every component is binary-safe including the tombstone flag of `Entry` (`rfile/entry.go:17`). |

<a id="sec-16"></a>

## 16. Matrix: HDFS (`SB-HDFS`)

Shoal publishes `hdfs.Client`, owned sequential input/output streams, metadata
snapshots, raw and Java/Hadoop-compatible typed reads/writes, recursive remove,
rename, cancellation, and deadlines. Authentication remains exclusively in
standard Hadoop configuration; neither Go, C, nor Python accepts credential
bytes. The internal backend remains the cancellation-safe implementation.

| ID | Sharkbite | Shoal Go | Shoal C ABI | Evidence | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

<a id="sec-19"></a>

## 19. Matrix: C++ public surfaces (`SB-CPP`)

**Scope: every public C++ declaration Sharkbite ships, not only the ones its
tests and examples happen to exercise.** Revision 4 scoped this section to
"surfaces used by tests and examples", which let unexercised public members
escape enumeration; that wording is withdrawn. A header under `include/` is
published to Sharkbite consumers whether or not the pinned tree calls it, so it
carries a compatibility obligation.

These rows do not gate the Python wheel — that gate is [§5](#sec-5) through
[§18](#sec-18) — but they do gate any claim that Shoal replaces Sharkbite as a
whole, and they are `required` rows under [§2.2](#sec-2) unless individually
marked `Not required` with a rationale.

The curated rows below cover the flat C API, the `TableOperations` factories,
`AuthInfo`, `Sink`, `Source`, and the test infrastructure — the surfaces with
named Shoal counterparts or named Sharkbite tests. The complete
declaration-level enumeration follows in [§19.2](#sec-19-2); where a member
appears in both, the curated row is normative and the generated row
cross-references it.

| ID | Sharkbite | Shoal Go | Shoal C ABI | Evidence | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SB-CPP-001 | `create_connector(instance, zks, username, password)` (`include/extern/accumulo.h:108`) | `accumulo.NewConnector` (`accumulo/connector.go:36`) | `shoal_connector_create` (`capi/include/shoal.h`) | `TestNewConnectorLifecycle` (`accumulo/connector_test.go:9`); `main()` in `capi/tests/lifecycle.c` uses `SHOAL_BOOTSTRAP_STATIC` | Behavior mismatch | The flat C entry point is ZooKeeper-only — four `char *` arguments, no bootstrap discriminator — while the only ABI construction test uses the static bootstrap. Same gap as [SB-CONN-001](#sec-7). |
| SB-CPP-015 | `free_connector(connector) -> int` (`include/extern/accumulo.h:111`) | `Connector.Close` (`accumulo/connector.go:138`) | `shoal_connector_free` (`capi/include/shoal.h`) | `main()` in `capi/tests/lifecycle.c` frees twice | Behavior mismatch | Sharkbite returns an `int` status and leaves the caller's pointer dangling; `shoal_connector_free` returns `void`, performs a best-effort close, and NULLs the variable. A port must stop checking the return value and stop reusing the pointer. |

<a id="sec-19-1"></a>

### 19.1 Semantic inventory: scope, exclusions, and completeness

Three successive scanners have been rejected by audit: revision 6's was
class-only, revision 7's truncated signatures and guessed duplicate mappings,
and revision 8's silently dropped whole public classes. Revision 9 fixes the
scope- and scanner-state defects that caused those drops and records, per
failure class, what went wrong and what now proves it fixed.

**What changed mechanically in revisions 9 through 11:**

| Failure class in the previous revision | Root cause | Fix and proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Six class forward declarations recorded as external-linkage variables (`include/data/constructs/coordinator/AccumuloInfo.h:79`, `TabletServerStatus.h:55`, `include/scanner/constructs/Results.h:33,35,37`, `include/utils/BackTrace.h:36`) | a declaration ending in `;` fell through to the data-member branch, which took the last identifier as a variable name | `class`, `struct`, `union`, and `enum` forward declarations are type declarations; when the pinned tree defines the type they are merged into that definition, and when it does not they are rows describing an opaque type |
| `using std::void_t;` recorded as an external-linkage variable (`include/utils/TryMoveCall.h:25`) | the same fall-through, because a using-declaration also ends in `;` | using-declarations, using aliases, namespace aliases, and `using namespace` directives are classified separately: an alias is a type contract, a using-declaration re-exports a name, a namespace alias is a spelling, and a directive declares nothing |
| Five public bit-field data members absent (`include/extern/accumulo_data.h:47,85,86,87,88`) | the declarator parser took the last identifier of a declaration, which is the bit-field width, so `unsigned deleted : 1;` produced no name | bit-field widths are stripped per declarator before the name is taken, and each named bit-field is one row that records the width as part of the ABI layout |
| A function-pointer typedef recorded as a callable free function (`include/jni/JVMLoader.h:91`) | `typedef jint (*registerNatives_t)(...)` looks callable to a parameter-list test | function-pointer `typedef`/`using` declarations are aliases; the row says the alias names a callback type and declares no callable |
| pybind11 macro invocations recorded as free functions (`include/jni/PythonBindings.h:49,51`) | an ALL-CAPS macro applied to arguments was parsed as a function definition when the macro is defined in another library | macro invocations at namespace scope are recorded and excluded with a rationale; macro **definitions** and macro-declared types keep their rows |
| `static` namespace-scope variables described as externally linked, process-wide objects | linkage was never recorded, so every global got the same note | each namespace-scope variable records its linkage; `static` ones are described as internal linkage with one copy per translation unit, and the affected divergence row is corrected |
| Twelve `friend std::ostream &operator<<` functions absent (`include/data/constructs/Key.h:289,298`, `include/data/constructs/KeyExtent.h:166`, `include/data/constructs/KeyValue.h:65,72`, `include/data/constructs/Range.h:142,160`, `include/data/constructs/rfile/RFile.h:193,207`, `include/data/constructs/rfile/SequentialRFile.h:221,235`, `include/data/constructs/server/RangeDefinition.h:86`) | `friend` was a skip word, so friend functions defined inside a class body were never recorded | friend functions and operators are enumerated as namespace-scope obligations found by argument-dependent lookup, with the befriending class named in the row; `friend class X;` declarations are not records, because they declare friendship rather than a type |
| Out-of-class member definitions counted as new free functions (`Sink<T>::push`, `TransportPool<Tr>::getTransporter`, `TableOperations<K, V>::createTable`, `Worker<T>::operator=`, and 12 more) | a qualified definition at namespace scope was parsed as a fresh declaration | qualified definitions are matched to their in-class declaration by owner and member name and merged into it; 16 such definitions are recorded as merged, with the in-class access reported |
| Protected members required (`TransportPool::createNewTransport`, `Sink::enqueue`, `Sink::exceedQueue`) | those rows came from the out-of-class definitions above, which carried no access | every declaration now carries its access label; 700 protected and 346 private members are excluded by rule and counted, and no row may correspond to a non-public declaration |
| Every public `utils::StringUtils` member (`include/utils/StringUtils.h:75-263`) absent | anonymous-namespace state was a counter reset only at file scope, so the `namespace { … }` block at lines 40-58 marked the rest of the file internal | anonymity is a property of each namespace frame, popped with the frame; `StringToBool`, the trims, the comparisons, and all four `join` overloads are enumerated |
| All of `writer::Sink` (`include/writer/Sink.h:43-82`) and `cclient::data::KeyAllocatorPool` (`include/data/constructs/rfile/AllocatorPool.h:42-52`) absent | a header was classified vendored when a vendor name appeared anywhere in its first 40 lines, so any header that merely *used* `moodycamel::` or included libhdfs3 was dropped | vendoring is decided by path and by the file's own license block, never by what it references |
| `Hdfs`, `HdfsInputStream`, `HdfsOutputStream` absent although they are Python-exposed | same misclassification | all three are Sharkbite-authored wrappers and are enumerated in full |
| Namespace-scope declarations absent (`IsEmpty`, the two JNI entry points, and eight globals) | three separate causes: trailing return types containing `==` failed the callable test; `extern "C" {` opened a brace that was not modelled, so nothing inside was at namespace scope; and namespace-scope variables were excluded by rule | trailing returns accept any expression, `extern "C"` is a transparent frame, and namespace-scope variables are enumerated as globals |
| `LOG_LEVEL` (`include/logging/Logger.h:62-70`) absent | only `enum`-introduced declarations were parsed, not `typedef enum { … } NAME;` | typedef-enums are parsed and named from the trailing alias, with ordinals `trace = 0 … off = 6` |
| Include guards emitted as required rows (9 rows) | guards were recognised only when valueless, so `#define KEY 1` looked like a constant | a `#define NAME` or `#define NAME 1` immediately preceded by `#ifndef NAME` or `#if !defined(NAME)` is a guard |

The revision-8 fixes that the audit confirmed are preserved unchanged: full
untruncated signatures with balanced parameter lists, evidence-proved duplicate
mappings, the `maj`/`min` declarator split, `TabletType` and `ScannerOptions`
ordinals, document-derived cross-reference anchors, the corrected `Key`
accessor citations, and the rescoped [SB-RFILE-005](#sec-15).

**Duplicate obligations are proved, not guessed.** A generated row is
`Not required` only when one of these holds, and the rule that fired is stated
in the row:

1. **Cited declaration** — a normative row cites this exact `header:line`.
2. **Bound overload** — the member is bound into Python at a specific
   `pysharkbite.cpp` line, the binding's explicit member-function-pointer cast
   (or `pybind11::init<>` argument list) matches this declaration's parameter
   list after qualifier normalisation, and a normative row cites that binding
   line. Where a binding carries no cast, the rule fires only if the class
   declares exactly one member with that name.

Everything else is a gap and carries its parity status. `SB-KEEP`,
`SB-UNSAFE`, `SB-DIV`, and `SB-GAP` entries can never discharge a matrix
obligation, because those tables are commentary, not matrix rows.

**Scope rules, applied mechanically and recorded per record:**

| Rule | Effect | Count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vendored by path: `include/extern/libhdfs3/**` (98 headers), `include/extern/thrift*/**` (50), `include/data/extern/concurrentqueue/**` (3, Cameron Desrochers' queue and Jeff Preshing's semaphore under Simplified BSD/zlib) | Excluded; **non-normative**, because Sharkbite redistributes rather than authors them, and a port replaces the dependency instead of the API | 152 headers, 29853 records |
| Vendored by the file's own license block: `include/utils/Uri.h` (Facebook/Folly) | Excluded on the same ground | included in the 152 |
| Internal linkage — anonymous namespace or private/protected nested type (`utils::{anonymous}::string_traits`) | Excluded: not reachable by a consumer, so not a contract | 11 records in live headers |
| Include guard — `#define NAME` or `#define NAME 1` immediately preceded by `#ifndef NAME` / `#if !defined(NAME)` | Excluded: the token's only contract is single inclusion of its own file | 182 records in live headers |
| Private or protected class members | Excluded from rows, but recorded with their access so the exclusion is auditable rather than invisible | 700 protected, 346 private |
| Out-of-class member definitions matching an in-class declaration | Merged into that declaration: the definition is not a second obligation | 16 merged |
| `friend` functions and operators declared or defined in a class body | **Included** as namespace-scope obligations: friendship is not access control, and callers reach them by argument-dependent lookup | 12 rows |
| Constructor initialiser continuations, inline bodies, trailing-return continuations, macro continuation lines | Not records at all: joined into the declaration they belong to | 0 records emitted |
| Everything else | One row each in [§19.2](#sec-19-2) | 2626 rows |

**A header is not vendored because it uses a vendored type.**
`include/utils/ConcurrentQueue.h` is Sharkbite's own Apache-licensed wrapper and
is enumerated; the redistributed queue lives in
`include/data/extern/concurrentqueue/` and is not. `include/writer/Sink.h`
queues into that vendored type and is enumerated. Any future exclusion must
name the file's own license or its vendored path, not a reference it makes.

**Internal linkage is not the same as internal API.** An anonymous-namespace
member is unreachable from another translation unit, so it is excluded. A
`static` or `inline` free function declared in a published header is different:
every file that includes the header gets a usable definition, so it is part of
what the header offers and is enumerated.

```text
rows = public members + enums + types with no public member

```

40, 49, 58, 66, and 74; `fromExtent`
(`include/data/constructs/tablet/TabletType.h:33`); the `Iterator` and
`BatchScanner` aliases (`include/scanner/impl/Scanner.h:162,164`); the
`BatchWriter` alias (`include/writer/impl/SinkImpl.h:107`);
`ROOT_TABLET_EXTENT` (`include/data/constructs/KeyExtent.h:250`); the seven
configuration macros (`include/data/constructs/ConfigurationOptions.h:23-31`);
and the six interconnect constants plus the `INTERCONNECT_TYPES` enum
(`include/interconnect/InterConnect.h:47-56`).

**Enum rows carry real value sets with correct ordinals.** Each of the 16 enum
rows lists every enumerator with its ordinal, explicit where the header assigns
one and derived sequentially otherwise. `LOG_LEVEL`
(`include/logging/Logger.h:62`) is `trace = 0; debug = 1; info = 2; warn = 3;
err = 4; critical = 5; off = 6`; `TabletType`
(`include/data/constructs/tablet/TabletType.h:28`) is `ROOT = 0; METADATA = 1;
USER = 2`; `ScannerOptions` (`include/scanner/ScannerOptions.h:23`) is
`BASIC_SCANNER = 0; ENABLE_HEDGED_READS = 1; ENABLE_RFILE_SCANNER = 2`; and
`TimeUnit` (`include/utils/StringUtils.h:29`) is `DAY = 0 … NANOSECOND = 5`.

**No usage-based exclusion.** An unused public API is still published, still
compiled against, and still a compatibility obligation under this section.
Destructors are assessed individually: where the owning class is bound into
Python the destructor is `Behavior mismatch` (15 rows), otherwise `Missing Go`
(124 rows), and 4 are duplicates of normative rows.

**Exception classes are additionally verified by hand.** `ClientException`
(both constructors, the public `errorCode` accessor, `~ClientException`,
`what()`, `getErrorCode()`, and the `INVALID_*` code macros), `HDFSException`,
`IllegalArgumentException`, `IllegalStateException`,
`IterationInterruptedException`, `NotServingException`, and
`VisibilityParseException` each have every public member enumerated, and each
cross-references its normative row in [§18](#sec-18) where one exists.
`APIException` (`include/interconnect/exceptions/APIException.h:23-24`)
declares `what()` under default `class` access — it is **private**, so
`APIException` has no public member and appears as a memberless-type row rather
than a member row. That asymmetry is a fact about the pinned header, not an
omission.

<a id="sec-19-3"></a>

### 19.3 Declaration-to-row verifier

The verifier is a mechanical check, re-run after every edit, that fails on any
of these conditions:

1. **Identity** — `rows ≠ members + enums + memberless types`.
2. **Orphan citation** — a `SB-CXX` row cites a `header:line` that the scanner
   did not record.
3. **Unenumerated declaration** — a scanned live declaration with no row.
4. **Artifact** — a row whose signature is a bare fragment rather than a
   declaration.
5. **Scope leak** — a row for a private or protected member, an anonymous
   namespace member, or a vendored header.
6. **Empty enum** — an enum row with no enumerator list.
7. **Unresolved duplicate** — a row whose member matches a normative row
   without a `Not required` status and an explicit cross-reference.
8. **Malformed row** — wrong column count, unbalanced backticks, or a status
   outside the six permitted values.
9. **Callable misclassification** — a function recorded as a constant or field.
10. **Silent drop** — a public member present in the header with no record.
11. **Truncated signature** — a row signature that is not a character-for-
    character copy of its scanner record, a record that ends mid-declaration,
    or a record with an unbalanced parameter list.
12. **Unproved duplicate** — a `Not required` duplicate whose stated rule
    cannot be re-derived from the cited evidence. `SB-KEEP`, `SB-UNSAFE`,
    `SB-DIV`, and `SB-GAP` entries are rejected as duplicate targets.
13. **Grouped declarator** — a declaration statement with more than one
    declarator that produced fewer rows than declarators.
14. **Enum ordinal** — ordinals that do not match the values recomputed from
    the header.
15. **Cross-reference anchor** — a `[SB-…](#sec-…)` link whose anchor is not
    the section the referenced row physically lives in.

Revision 9 adds five checks, each derived from a class of omission the seventh
audit found. These are **class coverage** checks: they compare the inventory
against the headers, not the document against itself, because every revision-8
defect was invisible to document-internal checking.

16. **Class coverage** — for every public class in a live header, the count of
    public members between its `public:` marker and its closing brace is
    recompared against the rows emitted for it. `writer::Sink` (10),
    `cclient::data::KeyAllocatorPool` (5), and `utils::StringUtils` (18,
    including all four templated `join` overloads) are asserted explicitly.
17. **Scope-state leak** — after every anonymous namespace closes, the next
    public declaration in that file must be enumerated. Any file with an
    anonymous namespace and zero live records after it fails.
18. **Vendored justification** — every excluded header must match a vendored
    path or carry a third-party license block in its own comment header. A
    header excluded because it *references* a vendored symbol fails, and the
    Python-exposed `Hdfs`, `HdfsInputStream`, and `HdfsOutputStream` wrappers
    are asserted present.
19. **Namespace-scope coverage** — declarations at namespace scope, including
    those inside `extern "C"` blocks and namespace-scope variables, must be
    enumerated. The ten declarations the audit named are asserted by line.
20. **Guard artifact** — no row may be a `#define` whose preceding directive is
    the matching `#ifndef`/`#if !defined`, in either the valueless or the
    `1`-valued spelling.

Revision 10 adds four more, each derived from a defect the ninth audit found.

21. **Memberless type** — a type recorded as having no public member is
    re-checked against templated and operator members before the row is
    emitted. `interconnect::CopyKey` is asserted to carry
    `operator()`.
22. **Conversion operator** — declarations of the form `operator T(...)` must be
    enumerated as operators, not dropped;
    `AccumuloInfoBuilder::operator AccumuloInfo &&` and
    `TabletServerStatusBuilder::operator TabletServerStatus &&` are asserted by
    line.
23. **Unevaluated value** — no enum or constant row may present a
    template-dependent or otherwise unevaluated initialiser as a numeric
    ordinal. Rows whose initialiser cannot be evaluated must say so and quote
    the source text.
24. **Narrative reconciliation** — every count stated in prose or in a metadata
    field (live-API headers, vendored headers, declaration-free headers,
    members, enums, memberless types, rows, required rows) must equal the value
    recomputed from the inventory and from the matrix rows. The check scans
    **every occurrence**, not one canonical sentence: it walks all non-row lines
    with their neighbours, extracts each numeric or spelled-out claim, and
    compares it with the derived value, so a stale figure in a revision-history
    bullet fails exactly like a stale figure in [§1](#sec-1). It also requires
    the header partition to be stated as arithmetic that sums
    (live + vendored + declaration-free = total) and every declaration-free
    header to be named.

Revision 11 adds three more, from the tenth audit:

25. **Friend function** — every `friend` function or operator declared or
    defined in a live header must have a row, and no `friend class` declaration
    may produce one. The twelve `friend operator<<` overloads are asserted by
    line.
26. **Out-of-class definition** — a qualified definition (`A<T>::m`) may not
    produce a row of its own when the class declares `m`; the definition is
    merged and the merge is recorded with the in-class access.
27. **Access classification** — no row may correspond to a protected or private
    declaration, and every excluded member must carry its access label in the
    inventory, so the exclusion can be re-derived rather than trusted.

Revision 12 adds four more, from the eleventh audit:

28. **Bit-field member** — every named bit-field in a live header must have its
    own row; the five in `include/extern/accumulo_data.h` are asserted by line.
29. **Typedef versus function** — no `typedef`/`using` declaration may be
    classified as a callable, and function-pointer aliases must say they name a
    callback type.
30. **Macro-invocation artifact** — an invocation of a macro defined outside the
    pinned tree may not produce a declaration row, while macro definitions and
    macro-declared types keep theirs.
31. **Linkage classification** — a namespace-scope variable declared `static`
    must be described as internal linkage with one copy per translation unit,
    and no row or divergence rationale may call it process-wide.

Revision 13 adds three more, from the twelfth audit:

32. **Forward declaration** — no `class`, `struct`, `union`, or `enum` forward
    declaration may be recorded as a variable or a function. Where the pinned
    tree defines the type, the declaration is merged into that definition and
    the merge names the defining line; where it does not, the row describes an
    opaque type.
33. **Using form** — using-declarations, using aliases, namespace aliases, and
    `using namespace` directives are classified distinctly, and none of them
    may be a variable.
34. **Namespace-variable population** — the count of namespace-scope variables
    and their linkage split are re-derived **from the headers by a second,
    independent walk** that tracks brace, namespace, and class depth without
    consulting the inventory, then compared with the inventory, with the matrix
    rows, and with every prose figure anywhere in the document. Agreement of two
    independent parsers plus the rows is the evidence; a claim that matches none
    of the derived numbers fails.

35. **Registration DSL** — a header that registers types or members through a
    binding DSL (`PYBIND11_EMBEDDED_MODULE`, `pybind11::class_`, `.def`) is a
    public surface even when it contains no C++ declaration. Every registration
    must have a row, and no such header may be counted declaration-free. The
    check walks each registration from its opening token until its parentheses
    balance, so a chained call that spans lines is one registration with one
    span, and it compares the row against that span rather than against the
    first line.
37. **Registration completeness** — for every registration, the row must cite
    the full span (`file:start-end` when it spans lines) and must contain the
    complete registered contract: the callable name, and every
    `pybind11::arg`/`"name"_a` keyword with its default token exactly as
    written. A row that keeps only the callable name, or that stops at a line
    break, fails.
36. **Unbuilt public header** — a header that no translation unit includes, or
    whose feature option defaults to `OFF`, may not be represented as a working
    capability anywhere in the document. Its rows must state the build
    exclusion, and any capability row that depends on it must cite the same
    evidence.

Checks 35 and 36 are enforced against the source, not the prose: check 35
re-scans every `PYBIND11_EMBEDDED_MODULE`, `pybind11::class_`, and `.def`
registration in every non-vendored header and requires one row each (35 in the
one such header), and check 36 re-counts references to that header across the
whole pinned tree and fails if the dead-code rationale ever becomes stale.

Result on this revision: **0 exceptions in all thirty-seven checks.** Checks 24
and 34 now scan every occurrence in the document rather than a single canonical
line, which is how revision 13's two surviving contradictions were found. In
addition,
every `pysharkbite.cpp` citation on a Python-visible row is verified to contain
the binding it claims.

<a id="sec-19-4"></a>

### 19.4 Matrix: dead embedded-module surface (`SB-EMB`)

`include/jni/PythonBindings.h` registers a complete pybind11 module,
`sharkbite_iterator`, that a server-side Python iterator would import: five
types and twenty-nine constructor and method registrations. Revision 14 treated
the header as declaration-free, because its two macro invocations are not C++
declarations. That was mechanically defensible and semantically wrong: a
registration DSL **is** a public surface, and silently dropping it hid a whole
Python API from the matrix.

It is enumerated here, one row per registration, with the single status the
evidence supports — `Not required` — because the surface is **pinned dead
code**:

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| No translation unit includes the header | zero references to `PythonBindings` anywhere in the pinned tree, including `CMakeLists.txt` |
| The feature is off by default | `option(PYTHON_ITERATOR_SUPPORT "Builds python iterator support." OFF)` (`CMakeLists.txt:37`) |
| The registered iterator type does not exist | `cclient::jni::python::PythonIterator` is never declared; `include/jni/PythonIterator.h:28-35` contains empty namespaces |
| Its implementation is commented out | `src/jni/PythonIterator.cpp:26-73` is one comment block; only empty namespaces remain |
| The executor it depends on is empty too | `include/jni/IteratorExecutor.h:28-33` declares nothing |
| Therefore it cannot compile as written | `include/jni/PythonBindings.h:89-95` takes the address of members of a type that does not exist |

**This is not a silent exclusion and not a claim of parity.** Every
registration has a row, so an auditor can see exactly what a revived module
would owe. If the project revives it, each row becomes an obligation and the
`Not required` rationale is withdrawn in the same change. The capability-level
consequence is recorded in [SB-SCAN-016](#sec-9), which no longer describes
server-side Python iterators as a working Sharkbite capability, and in
[SB-DIV-007](#sec-26).

**Registrations are recorded as spans, not as lines.** A pybind11 registration
is a chained call that may continue across lines, so each row is derived by
walking from the registration's opening token until its parentheses balance.
The citation is `file:start-end` whenever the registration is multi-line, and
the row repeats the callable name together with every `py::arg`/`"name"_a`
keyword and its default token exactly as written. Of the 35 registrations, 34
are single-line and one — `SB-EMB-010`, the five-argument `Key` constructor at
`include/jni/PythonBindings.h:65-66` — spans two lines and carries the module's
only keyword-argument contract: `row`, `columnfamily=""`,
`columnqualifier=""`, `columnvisibility=""`, and
`timestamp=9223372036854775807L`. Recording only the first line would have kept
the arity and lost the defaults. Check 37 ([§19.3](#sec-19)) re-derives every
span from the header and fails if a row cites a partial span, omits a keyword,
or drops a default.

<a id="sec-20"></a>

## 20. Matrix: cross-cutting semantics (`SB-XCUT`)

| ID | Concern | Sharkbite | Shoal Go | Shoal C ABI | Evidence | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SB-XCUT-001 | Object lifecycle / ownership | `shared_ptr` holders for most types; `unique_ptr` from `createScanner`/`createWriter`; raw owning `RFile*` from `RFileOperations::open`; `ZookeeperInstance` owns raw `ZooCache`/`ZooKeeper` pointers deleted in its destructor | Go GC + explicit `Close` on `Connector`, `BatchWriter`, `Instance` | Opaque handles; `*_close` then `*_free`; free implies best-effort close and NULLs the caller's variable (`capi/README.md`) | `TestConnectorRegistryLifecycle` (`cmd/shoal-capi/state_test.go`); `FoundationTests.test_connector_context_close_is_idempotent` and `test_connector_copy_is_explicitly_rejected` (`python/tests/test_foundation.py`); `main()` in `capi/tests/lifecycle.c` | Covered | Revision 49 defines deterministic Python context-manager ownership, idempotent close/free, non-copyable wrappers, and best-effort finalization. Explicit close remains required for prompt remote cleanup. |

| SB-XCUT-003 | Copied vs borrowed memory | `Key` holds raw `char *` buffers paired with `disown*` flags — `disownRow`/`row` (`include/data/constructs/Key.h:344-345`), `disownColumnFamily`/`colFamily` (`include/data/constructs/Key.h:352-354`), `disownColumnQualifier`/`colQualifier` (`include/data/constructs/Key.h:360-361`), `disownColumnVisibility`/`keyVisibility` (`include/data/constructs/Key.h:365-366`), toggled by the `setDisown*` methods (`include/data/constructs/Key.h:215-227`); callers can be handed borrowed buffers | All public byte accessors return defensive copies (`cloneRow`, `accumulo/discovery.go:266`; `Column.Family()`, `accumulo/scanner.go:56`; `Mutation.Row()`, `accumulo/mutation.go:33`) | `shoal_connector_config`, `shoal_scanner_config`, `shoal_range`, and `shoal_key_value_view` (`capi/include/shoal_types.h`) borrow inputs for the call only and borrow outputs until the owning result is freed | `TestDiscoveryInvalidationAndDefensiveCopies` (`accumulo/discovery_test.go`); `TestEffectiveTablePropertiesConcurrentCopyIsolation` (`accumulo/table_property_reads_test.go`); `FoundationTests.test_client_scan_copies_and_frees_owned_result` (`python/tests/test_foundation.py`); `main()` in `capi/tests/result_bridge.c` | Covered | All retained inputs and Python-visible results are copied. C result views are deliberately borrowed only until their named owner is freed; Python copies them before that free. |

The contract is exercised through direct Go tests and dynamically loaded C and C++ consumers. |

Linux CI supplies the gcc/ELF claim; native artifact tooling separately validates object export tables. |
| SB-XCUT-014 | C ABI build and CI | n/a | n/a | `scripts/cross_platform_artifacts.py`; `scripts/cross-platform-artifacts.ps1`; `TestSharedLibraryCABI`; `python/scripts/{build_release.py,verify_release.py,build_preview.py,verify_preview.py}` | Windows/amd64 builds `c-shared` and `c-archive` artifacts with recorded hashes, compiles/links/runs C11 and C++11 shared clients plus the C11 static lifecycle client, verifies ABI 1.18.0/capabilities and all 322 exports, and repeats clean wheel/sdist builds with identical hashes. Both macOS architectures cross-build the non-CGO command and reproducibly build/install explicitly unbundled tagged previews. | Behavior mismatch | The macOS previews prove package layout, imports, and safe missing-library behavior only. | SB-XCUT-015 | Live-cluster conformance | Live tests exist but are excluded from CI (`.github/workflows/ccpp.yml` runs only three no-cluster CTest targets) | All 90 `accumulo/` tests are unit tests with fake adapters (no build tags, no env gating, no testcontainers) | C tests use compile-time seams (`capi/tests/test_seam.h`) | `make test-hdfs` + `.github/workflows/hdfs-integration.yml` are the only live-service tests in Shoal, and they cover HDFS only | Missing Go | Neither project verifies Accumulo client behavior against a live cluster in CI. | SB-XCUT-017 | GIL behavior | pybind11 holds the GIL unless explicitly released; `Results.__anext__` resolves futures inline | Blocking Go C ABI calls contain no Python callbacks | The Python binding loads with `ctypes.CDLL`, which releases the GIL around foreign calls and reacquires it on return | `CrossCuttingCompiledTests.test_ctypes_releases_and_reacquires_gil_for_native_calls` (`python/tests/test_cross_cutting.py`) blocks in a tagged Go C ABI seam while another Python thread progresses, then performs a Python assertion after return | Covered | The binding uses `ctypes.CDLL`, never `PyDLL`: the GIL is released for each foreign call and reacquired before result copying, exception mapping, or callbacks into Python. |
| SB-XCUT-018 | Fork safety | Not documented; process-wide singleton pools make `fork()` unsafe | The Go runtime is not called in a fork child before exec | Inherited child-side use is explicitly unsupported; Python process guards raise `ForkSafetyError` before symbol resolution or native calls | `CrossCuttingCompiledTests.test_inherited_native_state_is_rejected_before_go_call` and `test_exec_subprocess_can_load_fresh_native_state` (`python/tests/test_cross_cutting.py`); `capi/README.md`; `python/README.md` | Covered | Raw C callers must exec before any child-side Shoal call. Python enforces that contract before symbol resolution or Go entry for inherited calls and new API construction; fresh exec-created subprocesses are supported. |
| SB-XCUT-019 | Symbol visibility and calling convention, Windows and macOS | n/a | n/a | `SHOAL_API` = `__declspec(dllexport)`/`__declspec(dllimport)`, `SHOAL_CALL` = `__cdecl`; `scripts/cross_platform_artifacts.py`; `TestSharedLibraryCABI` | Windows/amd64 PE export-table inspection finds all 322 declared `shoal_*` symbols; C11/C++11 clients dynamically and statically link and execute; the dynamic query verifies ABI 1.17.0 and 30 capabilities. macOS package previews contain no native library by construction. | Missing C ABI | Windows is verified on its native host. macOS header declarations and package tags are represented, but Mach-O exports, calling convention, native link, and runtime remain unsupported. @phrocker deferred Mach-O/native-link verification on 2026-08-20; it is optional for the current release. |

<a id="sec-21"></a>

## 21. Unsafe or defective Sharkbite behavior (do not reproduce)

Each item is a defect in the pinned Sharkbite release, not a contract. The
compatibility shim must implement the listed replacement instead of copying the
behavior. None of these may be silently "fixed" without recording the change
here, because some code depends on the broken shape.

| ID | Defect | Location | Why it is unsafe | Compatibility shim |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SB-UNSAFE-001 | `Authorizations.__str__`/`__repr__` dereference `vec.end()-1` and `vec.back()` on an empty vector | `pysharkbite.cpp:464-484` | Undefined behavior — `str(Authorizations())` can crash the interpreter. `Authorizations()` with no entries is the most common construction in the pinned tests. | Return `[ ]` for empty, `[ a, b ]` otherwise. Match the non-empty format exactly. |
| SB-UNSAFE-002 | `Value.get()` transcodes bytes to `str` | `pysharkbite.cpp:274` | Raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on binary values; silently corrupts data on lossy platforms. | Keep `get()` but decode with `errors='surrogateescape'`; add `get_bytes()` (already in the contract) and document `get_bytes()` as the correct accessor. |
| SB-UNSAFE-003 | `Key.getRow()`/`getColumnFamily()`/`getColumnQualifier()`/`getColumnVisibility()` return `str` with no bytes alternative | `pysharkbite.cpp:321-325` | Binary row keys — normal in Accumulo — are unreachable from Python and raise on decode. | Same `surrogateescape` rule plus new `*_bytes()` accessors. Additive, so existing code is unaffected. |
| SB-UNSAFE-004 | `Key(const char*, ...)` constructor truncates at the first NUL | `pysharkbite.cpp:299-300` | Silent data corruption for binary components. | Accept `bytes` and pass length explicitly through `shoal_bytes`. |
| SB-UNSAFE-005 | `BatchWriter.flush()` cannot be called with zero arguments | `pysharkbite.cpp:487` vs `include/writer/Sink.h:62` | The documented API is unusable; pybind11 does not inherit the C++ default. | Expose `flush(override: bool = False)`. |
| SB-UNSAFE-006 | `BatchScanner.fetchColumn(cf)` cannot be called with one argument | `pysharkbite.cpp:436` vs `include/scanner/Source.h:85` | Same class of defect; column-family-only fetching is unreachable. | Expose `fetchColumn(cf, cq=None)`. |
| SB-UNSAFE-007 | `AccumuloScanner.select_column` calls `fetchColumn` with the wrong arity on both branches | `sharkbite/__init__.py:140-144` | The helper never works: the `cq` branch passes one argument, the no-`cq` branch passes `None`. | Fix the branches; keep the method name and signature. |
| SB-UNSAFE-008 | `AccumuloIterator.__next__` consumes an entry from the underlying result set and *then* raises `StopIteration` once `_chunkCounter >= _chunkSize`, discarding the entry it just pulled | `sharkbite/__init__.py:190-194`; `pandashark/pandassharkbite.py:27-34` | Two distinct defects. (1) **Boundary-row loss**: the row fetched on the chunk-limit call is consumed from the result set and never returned to anyone, so every chunk boundary silently drops one entry. (2) **Truncation for direct users**: `AccumuloScanner.get(...)` hands the iterator straight to callers (`sharkbite/__init__.py:146-154`), and nothing there ever calls `nextBatch()`, so a plain `for kv in scanner.get(row, chunksize=1000)` stops after 1000 entries and reports success. `nextBatch()` **is** called — but only by `pandashark`'s `DataFrameIterator.__next__` on `StopIteration` (`pandashark/pandassharkbite.py:60-72`), which is why the pandas path yields successive frames while the direct path truncates. | Do not reproduce either defect. Read the boundary entry once and return it; treat `chunksize` as a batching hint that never terminates iteration; keep `nextBatch()` as a no-op-compatible method so `DataFrameIterator` keeps working. Record as [SB-DIV-006](#sec-26) because it changes result counts for both paths. |
| SB-UNSAFE-009 | `AccumuloIterator.__init__` is defined twice; the first definition is dead | `sharkbite/__init__.py:174-181` | The one-argument constructor documented by the first definition does not exist at runtime. | Provide `__init__(self, scanner, chunkSize=0)`. |
| SB-UNSAFE-010 | `AccumuloScanner` is defined twice in the same module; the first definition (with a `pass` constructor) is dead | `sharkbite/__init__.py:60-63` and `126-148` | `AccumuloBase.to_scanner()` silently depends on which definition wins. | Single definition. |
| SB-UNSAFE-011 | `AuthInfo::operator=` fails to copy the password | `include/data/constructs/security/AuthInfo.h:60-67` | Copy-assigned credentials silently authenticate with an empty password. | Shoal's `Credentials.clone()` copies everything (`accumulo/credentials.go:44`). Do not reproduce. |
| SB-UNSAFE-012 | `CompressorFactory::create()` constructs but never throws its error | `include/data/constructs/compressor/CompressorFactory.h:39-48` | An unsupported codec silently falls through instead of failing. | Fail loudly with `ClientException`. |
| SB-UNSAFE-013 | `RFileOperations::open` returns a raw owning pointer while its four siblings return `shared_ptr` | `include/data/constructs/rfile/RFileOperations.h:45` | Guaranteed leak from Python, which never deletes it. | Single owning model; close deterministically via context manager. |
| SB-UNSAFE-014 | `CompressorFactory::getZlibCompressor()` leaks a process-wide singleton | `include/data/constructs/compressor/CompressorFactory.h:35` | Intentional leak; harmless but not a contract. | Do not reproduce. |
| SB-UNSAFE-015 | `TableRates` registers `query_rate_byte` four times and never registers an ingest-rate property | `pysharkbite.cpp:110-120` | Three registrations are dead; the property set does not match the getters. | Register each property once; keep every getter name. |
| SB-UNSAFE-016 | `tableOps.import(...)` and `IterInfo.class()` use Python reserved words | `pysharkbite.cpp:93` (`IterInfo.class`), `pysharkbite.cpp:241` (`tableOps.import`) | Unreachable through normal attribute syntax. | Keep the reserved-word names for `getattr` users and add usable aliases. |
| SB-UNSAFE-017 | `AccumuloWriter.__del__` performs network I/O during interpreter teardown | `sharkbite/__init__.py:128-129` | Exceptions are swallowed; module globals may already be torn down; writes can be silently lost. | Keep a best-effort `__del__`, emit a `ResourceWarning` when it has real work to do, and document `with`/`close()`. |
| SB-UNSAFE-018 | Server-side update errors are never surfaced to Python | `pysharkbite.cpp:486-497` (no failure accessor on the `Sink` binding) | Rejected mutations look like successful writes. | Surface `MutationRejectionError` through `ClientException`; see SB-WRITE-010 and [§26](#sec-26). |
| SB-UNSAFE-019 | `ZookeeperInstance` owns raw `ZooCache`/`ZooKeeper` pointers with manual `delete` | `include/data/constructs/client/zookeeperinstance.h` | Inconsistent with the rest of the API and easy to double-free. | Shoal's `Instance.Close()` is idempotent (`accumulo/instance.go:143`). |
| SB-UNSAFE-020 | Committed build artifacts in the test tree (`test/zookeeper/construct_test`, `test/zookeeper/testInstance`) and an empty `test/services/CMakeLists.txt` | `test/` | The mock-server test path is dead; the harness cannot be trusted as evidence. | Ignore as evidence; port the behavior into live-cluster conformance instead. |
| SB-UNSAFE-021 | `AccumuloDataset.coerce` calls `key.getKey().getValue()` — `Key` has no `getValue` binding (`pysharkbite.cpp:297-326` defines `getRow`, `getColumnFamily`, `getColumnQualifier`, `getColumnVisibility`, `getTimestamp` only) | `sharkbite/torch.py:24-36` | Every default (no `user_lambda`) coercion raises `AttributeError` inside the `try`, prints the exception, and **returns `0`**. A PyTorch training loop therefore trains on an all-zero tensor stream while looking healthy. The same swallow-and-return-0 path hides genuine user-lambda errors. | Call `keyvalue.getValue()` on the `KeyValue`, not on the `Key`; propagate coercion errors instead of returning a sentinel. Both changes alter observable output — recorded as [SB-DIV-011](#sec-26). |
| SB-UNSAFE-022 | `AccumuloValueDataset.__init__` calls `super.__init__(cluster, table, start, end)` — missing parentheses on `super`, and four positional arguments against a nine-parameter base signature | `sharkbite/torch.py:64-66` vs `sharkbite/torch.py:14` | Constructing `AccumuloValueDataset` always raises `AttributeError: 'super' object has no attribute '__init__'`; even with `super()`, the argument list does not match `AccumuloDataset.__init__`. The class is unusable in the pinned release. | Implement it correctly (`super().__init__(...)` with the full argument list). Because no working program can depend on the broken behavior, this is a defect fix, not a divergence. |
| SB-UNSAFE-023 | `AccumuloBase.set_threads` mutates `_threads` after scanners and writers have already been constructed, and `AccumuloBase.to_scanner` forwards neither `_threads` nor a live connector | `sharkbite/__init__.py:21-22,52-53,136-138` | `AccumuloScanner.__init__` calls `createScanner(self._auths, self._threads)` once at construction, so `set_threads` after construction silently has no effect; `to_scanner()` builds a brand-new `AccumuloScanner` from the stored credentials, discarding the caller's thread count and opening a second connector. Users get a different parallelism than they asked for and twice the connections. | Apply `set_threads` lazily at scan time and forward the current thread count (and connector) through `to_scanner`. Document the changed connection count. |

(3) The first statement is `flattenedText.at(flattenedText.size() - 1)`, so an empty row computes `size() - 1` on a `size_t`, wraps to its maximum, and throws `std::out_of_range` - a different exception from the documented one. (4) It tests the trailing `<` **before** looking for a `;`, so a bounded tablet whose end row itself ends in `<` - a legal Accumulo row - decodes as a different table with no end row: `createMetadataEntry("1", "k<")` produces `1;k<`, which comes back as table `1;k`. The encoder and the decoder in the same class do not round trip. | Return errors, index with `int`, and let the bounded form win. `ParseTabletExtent` rejects an empty row and a row with no separator with `ErrInvalidTabletExtent`, finds the separator with `strings.IndexByte`, which has no width limit, and recognises the trailing `<` only when the row has no `;` at all; `TestParseTabletExtentHandlesLongRows` decodes a 40000-byte end row and a 40000-byte table id, and `TestParseTabletExtentDecodesMetadataRows` round trips an end row ending in `<` (`accumulo/tablet_extent_test.go`). |
| SB-UNSAFE-051 | `KeyExtent::setPrevEndRow(char*, size_t)` drops the first byte and underflows on an empty value | `include/data/constructs/KeyExtent.h:200-202` | The buffer overload builds the row as `std::string(text + 1, text_len - 1)`. For an empty value `text_len - 1` wraps to `SIZE_MAX` and the constructor is asked for a string of that length; for a non-empty value the first byte is discarded without a check that one was meant to be there. The `std::shared_ptr<Value>` overload - the one the public `KeyExtent(flattenedText, prevEndRow)` constructor uses - forwards straight into it, so an empty previous end row read from the metadata table takes the wrapping path. | Copy what the caller gave. `TabletExtent.SetPrevRow` copies the slice as it is, and an absent bound is `nil` rather than a value that has to be decoded; `TestTabletExtentCloneAndSetters` (`accumulo/tablet_extent_test.go`) covers the empty and nil cases. |
| SB-UNSAFE-052 | `KeyValue::operator==` compares object identity, not content, so separately constructed equal-content entries compare unequal | `src/data/constructs/KeyValue.cpp:69-73` | The body is `((Key *)key->getStream().get() == (Key *)(rhs.key->getStream().get())) && (value == rhs.value)`. The first term compares two **addresses** - `Key::getStream()` returns `shared_from_this()`, so `.get()` is the key's own address - and the second compares two `shared_ptr<Value>` handles, which is again identity. Two entries decoded independently from the same bytes therefore compare unequal. A copy-constructed entry shares both handles and compares equal, while assignment shares the key but deep-copies the value and therefore compares unequal, making equality depend on construction history rather than content. Nothing about the key's row, column, timestamp or the value's bytes is read. | Compare content. `KeyValue.Equal` is `Compare(other) == 0`, and `Compare` orders by `Key.Compare` and then by the value bytes; `TestKeyValueEqualComparesContentNotIdentity` (`accumulo/data_model_test.go`) pins that two separately built entries with the same bytes are equal. |
| SB-UNSAFE-053 | `KeyValue::operator<` inherits an incomplete key ordering, and `operator=` shares the key while copying the value | `src/data/constructs/KeyValue.cpp:47-67` | `operator<` evaluates `*(Key *)key->getStream().get() < *(Key *)(rhs.key->getStream().get())`. Because `StreamInterface` is a public non-virtual base of `Key`, the C-style base-to-derived cast may perform the standard pointer adjustment; base order is irrelevant. The indirect conversion is not the defect. The result still inherits `Key::operator<`, which ignores the timestamp ([SB-UNSAFE-046](#sec-21)), while `operator==` compares identity ([SB-UNSAFE-052](#sec-21)), so ordering and equality contradict each other. `operator=` compounds it: it assigns `key = other.key`, sharing one `Key` between two entries, while deep-copying the value - so mutating one entry's key mutates the other's. | Compare and copy values. `KeyValue.Compare` calls `Key.Compare` and then compares the value bytes, `Less` and `Equal` are defined from it, and `Clone` and `NewKeyValue` copy both halves; `TestKeyValueCloneAndSetters` (`accumulo/data_model_test.go`) pins that a clone shares no storage. |
| SB-UNSAFE-054 | `KeyValue::setKey` ignores its ownership argument and `hasOwnerShip()` is hard-coded to `false` | `src/data/constructs/KeyValue.cpp:32`, `include/data/constructs/KeyValue.h:50-57` | The setter is declared `setKey(std::shared_ptr<Key> k, bool set_ownership = false)` and defined as `{ key = k; }` - the flag is never read. Its companion accessor is `inline bool hasOwnerShip() { return false; }`, a constant. A caller who asks the entry to take ownership is told, truthfully by accident, that it did not; the pair documents a lifetime contract the class does not implement, and any code branching on it takes the same branch forever. | Own the key outright. `KeyValue.SetKey` copies the key it is given and the entry owns it, so there is no flag to honour and no accessor to lie; `TestKeyValueCloneAndSetters` (`accumulo/data_model_test.go`) pins that the entry does not alias the caller's key. |
| SB-UNSAFE-055 | `Column` declares two `operator==`, one virtual and const, the other neither | `include/data/constructs/column.h:71,97` | The class declares `virtual bool operator==(const Column &other) const` and, later in the same class body, `bool operator==(const Column &other)` - non-virtual, non-const, defined inline. Overload resolution picks the second whenever the left operand is non-const, which is the common case, so a derived class that overrides the virtual one is silently bypassed. The two bodies happen to compare the same three fields today, so the duplication is invisible until someone changes one of them or subclasses `Column`. | Publish one comparison. `Column.Equal` is `Compare(other) == 0` and `Compare` orders family, qualifier and visibility, so there is a single answer and a single definition; `TestColumnCompareOrdersEveryComponent` (`accumulo/data_model_test.go`) pins that `Equal`, `Less` and `Compare` agree. |
| SB-UNSAFE-056 | Streaming a `KeyValue` prints the key's address and drops the value | `include/data/constructs/KeyValue.h:65-73` | The body is `out << "key is " << rhs.key;`, and `rhs.key` is a `std::shared_ptr<Key>`. `Key` declares stream operators for `Key &` and `Key *` but none for the shared pointer, so overload resolution selects the standard library's `operator<<(basic_ostream &, const shared_ptr<Y> &)`, which prints `get()` - a raw address. A printed entry is therefore `key is 0x55f3...`: none of the row, column, visibility or timestamp appears, the value is never streamed at all, and the one token that does appear changes between runs. The pointer overload forwards here and inherits it. | Render both halves. `KeyValue.String` formats the key through `Key.String` and reports the value's length rather than its bytes, which may be binary; `TestKeyValueStringNamesBothHalves` (`accumulo/data_model_test.go`) pins that the rendering names the key and the value size and contains no address. |

## 23. Gap ledger and ordered prerequisites

Work proceeds strictly in stage order. A stage may not start until the previous
stage is complete for the rows it depends on.

This ledger is the ordered-gap deliverable of Shoal issue
[#81](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/81). Every `SB-GAP-*` entry
below without an existing issue link needs one filed and linked back to #81
before its stage starts; #81 stays open until every stage-1 through stage-4
entry is either closed or reclassified in [§26](#sec-26).
