### 23.6 Pin discipline for in-flight work

Row statuses describe the pinned Shoal commit in [§1](#sec-1) and nothing else.
An open pull request — however complete, however green its CI — never changes a
row from `Missing Go` or `Missing C ABI`, and never contributes evidence: a
test that does not exist on `main` cannot be named by a `Covered` row under the
[§2](#sec-2) gate. In-flight work is recorded only in this ledger and in
[§23.5](#sec-23-5).

When such a PR merges, the repin is a deliberate, auditable step:

1. Update the `Shoal reference` row in [§1](#sec-1) to the new verified
   `origin/main` SHA and update the `§3.2` inventory counts.
2. Re-audit the affected rows against the merged code and its **named** tests,
   applying the [§4.2](#sec-4) rules — including "unproven equivalence counts
   as difference". Landing an API is not the same as proving Sharkbite
   semantics; expect most rows to move `Missing Go` → `Behavior mismatch`
   rather than straight to `Covered`.
3. Re-run the mechanical count extraction and update [§25](#sec-25) in the same
   change.
4. Record any semantics that cannot be reproduced as a divergence in
   [§26](#sec-26). Note that a divergence is **not** contingent on a pull
   request: [SB-DIV-016](#sec-26) and [SB-DIV-013](#sec-26) exist because
   Accumulo removed the capability upstream, and PR
   [#98](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/pull/98) was withdrawn rather
   than merged. Nothing in this ledger queues withdrawn work. Both are now
   settled without code: [SB-DIV-016](#sec-26) was approved on 2026-08-19 and
   [SB-DIV-013](#sec-26) is subsumed by it.

<a id="sec-24"></a>

## 24. Live-cluster conformance requirements

All 94 Go tests in `accumulo/` are unit tests driven by fake adapters: a search
for build tags, `testing.Short()`, environment gating, and testcontainers in
`accumulo/*_test.go` returns nothing. The only live-service coverage in Shoal is
HDFS (`make test-hdfs`, `.github/workflows/hdfs-integration.yml`). Sharkbite's
own live tests are equally excluded from its CI. Therefore **no row whose
semantics are defined by a real tablet server may be marked `Covered` on unit
evidence alone**.

Rows that require live-cluster evidence before they can close:

Some rows below are already `Covered` at the Go and C ABI layers. That status
records what Shoal's own layers prove; the live-cluster test additionally
validates the end-to-end Python shim against a real tablet server. A row that is
not yet `Covered` cannot be closed by a live test alone either — it needs both.

| Area | Rows | What must be proven against a real Accumulo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authentication | SB-CONN-012, SB-KEEP-021 | Bad credentials and dropped users raise the mapped exception. |
| Visibility | SB-SEC-018, SB-KEEP-017 | Cells are filtered exactly as `test/python/TestAuthorizations.py` asserts. |
| Server-side iterators | SB-SCAN-006, SB-SCAN-016 | A configured iterator actually transforms results. |
| Tablet movement | SB-SCAN-026, SB-KEEP-022 | Scans survive real splits and migrations. |
| Write failures | SB-WRITE-010, SB-WRITE-011, SB-WRITE-012 | Constraint violations, authorization failures, and ambiguous commits behave as modeled. |
| Binary safety | SB-XCUT-004, SB-GAP-T-003 | Non-UTF-8 and NUL-containing components survive a real round trip. |
| Range semantics | SB-DATA-020…SB-DATA-024, SB-KEEP-005, SB-KEEP-006 | Empty, `None`, and whole-row ranges return the pinned row counts. |
| Scale and streaming | SB-XCUT-010, SB-GAP-T-006 | 250k-row write and scan complete without materializing the result set. |
| Table lifecycle | SB-TABLE-001…SB-TABLE-003, SB-KEEP-012, SB-KEEP-013 | `exists`/`create`/`remove` sequencing matches, including the `create` returning `False` case. |

Minimum harness: an ephemeral single-node Accumulo 4 plus ZooKeeper (the role
Sharkbite's `test/19x/st` SMAC project played), driven from CI, with the ported
`test/python/*.py` suite as the acceptance gate.

### 25.3 Reading the counts

**Exactly 355 rows are `Covered`: [SB-XCUT-012](#sec-20), the twelve configuration/topology rows completed in revision 24, the 31 RFile/stream rows completed in revision 25, the 17 data-model value rows completed in revision 26, the five buffered-writer rows completed in revisions 28 and 45, the four row-bounded flush/constraint rows completed in revision 29, the connector invalidation/cancellation rows completed in revision 30, the eight high-level client rows completed in revision 31, the five high-level scanner rows completed in revision 32, the four compatibility-error rows completed in revision 34, the twelve streaming cursor rows completed in revision 36, the 31 column-visibility rows completed in revision 38, the 22 equivalent owned-key rows completed in revision 42, the named-locality-group RFile row plus 24 HDFS rows completed in revision 44, the two logging rows completed in revision 45, the 38 table/namespace/security rows completed in revision 48, the twelve issue-196 cross-cutting rows completed in revision 49, the 60 required Python data-model and iterator-descriptor rows completed in revision 50, the five package/import rows completed in revision 51, the eleven RFile/HDFS/logging/error rows completed in revision 52, nineteen Python-visible scanner/writer rows completed in revision 53, the 28 configuration/credential/connector/session/dynamic-attribute rows completed in revision 54, and the controlled Linux manylinux release row completed in revision 56; revision 55 changes scope only; SB-WRITE-010 is the separately approved SB-DIV-005 divergence.** Capability discovery, configuration/topology, RFile, the supported data-value surface, the high-level buffered writer, table maintenance, connector controls, and bounded scan streaming are
now exported end to end: Go pins the append-only bitset contract, and linked C
and C++ consumers exercise them through the shared library. Every other
previously-claimed coverage row still needs either a live-cluster parity test
or a shim-level behavioral proof.

The raw inventory still contains 2206 `Missing Go` rows, including 2189
historical C++ members in [§19.2](#sec-19-2). Revision 52 does not relabel those
members as implemented: it classifies the legacy C++ compatibility surface as
`Optional`, because Python compatibility and the stable C ABI do not require a
source-compatible recreation of Sharkbite internals. Six `Missing Go`
rows remain in the required core.

`Behavior mismatch` (118) remains the detailed evidence bucket; 39 of those
rows are required blockers and the rest belong to optional or not-required
surfaces. `Intentional divergence` (98) is
dominated by one upstream fact: 82 rows are cluster-status accessors Accumulo
itself deleted ([§14](#sec-14), [SB-DIV-016](#sec-26)). @phrocker approved that
decision on 2026-08-19; the other sixteen divergence rows have their own named,
dated approvals, so all 98 satisfy the scope gate. [SB-CONN-007](#sec-7), the
`getStatistics()` entry point that reaches them, is not in that approved set and
is still counted in `Missing Go`. `Missing C ABI` (75) includes pandas (20),
packaging/import scaffolding (3), PyTorch (9), the complete-member inventory
(41), the remaining cross-cutting row (1), and the remaining curated-C++ row
(1); none are required after applying the scope ADR.

Revision 41 changes 25 statuses without changing the
inventory. Shoal completed the column and entry value types.
`accumulo.Column` gained the visibility component the pinned type carries, so a
column selection can name a family, a qualifier and a visibility; the new
component reaches the scan wire in `TColumn.ColumnVisibility` rather than being
stored and dropped. It also gained copying setters and one comparison,
`Compare`, ordering family, then qualifier, then visibility, with `Less` and
`Equal` derived from it. `accumulo.KeyValue` gained a copying constructor, a
deep `Clone`, copying setters, a `String` form that names both halves, and a
content comparison. Twenty-five [§19.2](#sec-19-2) members move from
`Missing Go` to `Missing C ABI` under rule 2 of [§4.2](#sec-4); five stay
`Missing Go` - the `Column` destructor, the two `write` stream methods and
`getStream`, which are the RFile wire format `internal/rfile` implements, and
`hasOwnerShip`, which reports a flag the pinned class never sets
([SB-GAP-GO-019](#sec-23)). Auditing the pinned types proved five defects,
recorded in [§21](#sec-21) rather than reproduced:
[SB-UNSAFE-052](#sec-21), where `KeyValue::operator==` compares the two key
addresses and the two value handles, so independently built entries with
identical bytes are unequal while copy-constructed entries sharing both handles
are equal; [SB-UNSAFE-053](#sec-21), where `operator<` inherits `Key`'s
incomplete ordering and `operator=` shares one key between two entries;
[SB-UNSAFE-054](#sec-21), where `setKey` ignores its ownership argument and
`hasOwnerShip()` is hard-coded to `false`; and [SB-UNSAFE-055](#sec-21), where
`Column` declares a virtual const `operator==` and a second non-virtual
non-const one that wins for non-const operands. [SB-UNSAFE-056](#sec-21)
completes the set: streaming an entry prints the key's address and never
prints the value. No row became `Covered` and the row population is
unchanged.

Revision 42 changes 36 statuses without changing the inventory. The merged public `accumulo.Key` constructors, copied setters, owned getters, comparison predicates, deletion/timestamp state, and size queries all move out of `Missing C ABI`: 22 move to `Covered`, while the nine inconsistent comparison/operator rows in [SB-UNSAFE-046](#sec-21) and the five capacity-reporting rows in [SB-UNSAFE-048](#sec-21) move to `Behavior mismatch` because the safe Shoal semantics deliberately differ from the pinned defects. ABI 1.15.0 capability 26 adds synchronized owned handles, binary-safe copied inputs, independently owned outputs, stable invalid-handle/allocation errors, C11/C++11 linked runtime coverage, and race evidence.

Revision 40 changes no status and no count at all: it mirrors the first
**approved** divergence in this document. @phrocker approved
[SB-DIV-016](#sec-26) on 2026-08-19 on Shoal issue
[#81](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/81#issuecomment-5343583850),
fixing the compatibility behavior for the cluster status and monitoring surface:
`connector.getStatistics()` raises a stable `NotImplementedError`, never returns
a fabricated or partially populated status object, is never surfaced as a
retryable `ClientException`, and capability discovery never advertises
cluster-status support ([§14](#sec-14)). Approving it reclassified nothing: the
82 rows it covers already carried `Intentional divergence (approval required)`,
and approval state lives in [§26](#sec-26) rather than in the status column, so
the row population, the section totals, and every classification are unchanged.
[SB-CONN-007](#sec-7), the entry point the decision names, keeps `Missing Go`:
the approval fixes what it must do, and the shim that raises is buildable
Python work. No row became `Covered` — an approved divergence records a
capability that will never exist, not one that has been delivered. The approval
creates two new obligations, both above the ABI: the raising shim
([SB-GAP-P-006](#sec-23)) and the conformance tests that pin it
([SB-GAP-T-009](#sec-23)).

plain strings so the tablet that ends a table sorts first among its tablets;
[SB-UNSAFE-050](#sec-21), where the metadata-row decoder throws a raw pointer

Revisions 1–9 (333, 368, 385, 473, 542, 2358, 2938, 3029, and 3175 rows, with

Revision 16 answers the fifteenth audit, which found one registration contract
recorded incompletely:

- **`SB-EMB-010` was truncated at a line break.** The `Key` constructor
  registration spans `include/jni/PythonBindings.h:65-66`, and its second line
  carries the entire keyword-argument contract: `row`, `columnfamily=""`,
  `columnqualifier=""`, `columnvisibility=""`, and
  `timestamp=9223372036854775807L`. The row cited line 65 only and stopped at
  the comma, which recorded the arity but dropped the defaults — exactly the
  class of loss that [§4.2](#sec-4) forbids for Python-visible rows.
- **The enumerator is now span-based.** Each registration is walked from its
  opening token until its parentheses balance, so a chained call that spans
  lines is one registration with one span. All 35 registrations were re-derived
  this way: 34 are single-line and one, `SB-EMB-010`, spans two lines. Every
  row now cites `file:start-end` where the span is multi-line and repeats the
  registered keyword names and defaults verbatim.
- **Counts and statuses are unchanged** — 35 rows, all `Not required` — because
  the audit found a truncation, not an omission. Fourteen row texts changed;
  the registration population did not.
- **Check 37 is added** and enforces this against the source: for every
  registration it compares the row's cited span with the derived span and
  requires every `"name"_a` keyword and default token to appear in the row.

Revision 15 answered the fourteenth audit, which found a semantic
misclassification rather than an arithmetic one:

- **A whole Python surface was dropped as "declaration-free".**
  `include/jni/PythonBindings.h` registers the `sharkbite_iterator` module: 5
  types and 29 constructor and method registrations. Revision 14 treated the
  header as declaration-free because pybind11 registrations are not C++
  declarations. That is mechanically true and semantically wrong, so all 35
  registrations are now enumerated in [§19.4](#sec-19-4), one row each.
- **They are `Not required`, and the evidence is exhaustive, not asserted.** No
  translation unit includes the header (zero references tree-wide);
  `PYTHON_ITERATOR_SUPPORT` defaults to `OFF` (`CMakeLists.txt:37`);
  `cclient::jni::python::PythonIterator` is never declared
  (`include/jni/PythonIterator.h:28-35`); its implementation is commented out
  (`src/jni/PythonIterator.cpp:26-73`); `include/jni/IteratorExecutor.h:28-33`
  is empty; and `PythonBindings.h:89-95` therefore takes the address of members
  of a type that does not exist, so the module cannot compile. Each row says so
  and says what happens if the module is revived: every row becomes an
  obligation and the rationale is withdrawn.
- **[SB-SCAN-016](#sec-9) no longer claims a working capability.** It was
  `Missing Go` and called "the single largest functional gap", which asserted
  that Sharkbite performs server-side Python iteration. It does not. The row is
  now `Not required` with the same five citations, and it separates what does
  ship — the client-side `PythonIterInfo` descriptor bound at
  `pysharkbite.cpp:96-104`, whose rows keep their obligations — from the dead
  runtime. [SB-DIV-007](#sec-26) is rescoped accordingly: choosing not to build
  server-side execution is a decision about new capability, not a regression.
- **Two verifier checks are added** so the class of error cannot recur: check
  35 requires registration-DSL surfaces to be enumerated and forbids counting
  such a header declaration-free; check 36 forbids any working-capability claim
  for a header no translation unit includes.
- **The header partition changes accordingly**: 205 headers hold rows, 152 are
  vendored, 6 are declaration-free, and 205 + 152 + 6 = 363.

Revision 14 answered the thirteenth audit, which found two mechanical
contradictions left in prose after revision 13 corrected the rows:

- **The header partition did not sum.** [§1](#sec-1) said 204 headers carry
  live public API and 152 are vendored, then called the remainder 6. The
  remainder is **7**, because `include/jni/PythonBindings.h` joined that set in
  revision 12 when its two pybind11 macro invocations stopped counting as
  declarations. The partition is now stated as arithmetic —
  `204 + 152 + 7 = 363` — and all seven declaration-free headers are named:
  `include/data/constructs/tables/tables.h`,
  `include/interconnect/Connector.h`,
  `include/interconnect/transport/TransportIdentifiers.h`,
  `include/jni/IteratorExecutor.h`, `include/jni/PythonBindings.h`,
  `include/jni/PythonIterator.h`, and `include/python/TableOps.h`.
- **A revision-history bullet still claimed seven `static` namespace-scope
  variables.** There are **five** — `ROOT_EXTENT`, `syncBarrier`,
  `ACCUMULO_COORDINATOR`, `MASTER_COORDINATOR`, and `CLUSTER_COORDINATOR` —
  because revision 13 removed the six forward declarations and the
  using-declaration that had been miscounted as variables. Every sentence in
  the document that states a variable or linkage count now agrees with the
  source.
- **The two checks that should have caught this are rewritten.** Checks 24 and
  34 previously compared one canonical sentence; they now scan every non-row
  line, extract numeric and spelled-out claims with their context, and compare
  against values derived twice — once from the inventory and once by an
  independent walk of the headers that tracks brace, namespace, and class
  depth. Row content is unchanged from revision 13; this revision is prose and
  verifier only.

Revision 13 answered the twelfth audit, which rejected two classification
defects that turned type and name declarations into phantom data gaps:

- **Six class forward declarations were counted as external-linkage
  variables.** `class AccumuloInfoBuilder;`, `class TabletServerStatusBuilder;`,
  `class ResultBlock;`, `class ResultIter;`, `class Results;`, and
  `class TraceResolver;` each ended in a semicolon and fell through to the
  data-member branch, which took the trailing identifier as a variable name.
  The pinned tree defines all six — at `AccumuloInfo.h:151`,
  `TabletServerStatus.h:141`, `Results.h:44`, `Results.h:171`, `Results.h:254`,
  and `BackTrace.h:90` — so each declaration is now merged into its definition
  and named in the exclusion ledger. A forward declaration of a type the tree
  never defines would still get a row, described honestly as an opaque type.
- **`using std::void_t;` was counted as a variable.** It is a
  using-declaration: it re-exports a name into `utils` and declares no object.
  The four using forms are now separated — type alias, using-declaration,
  namespace alias, and `using namespace` directive — and only the first two
  carry rows.
- **The namespace-variable population is now derived, not asserted.** The
  document claimed 15 variables with 7 `static`; the real population is **8**
  variables, **5** of them `static` with internal linkage
  (`ROOT_EXTENT`, `syncBarrier`, `ACCUMULO_COORDINATOR`, `MASTER_COORDINATOR`,
  `CLUSTER_COORDINATOR`) and **3** `extern` with external linkage
  (`cachedLocators`, `CLIENT_ERROR_CODES`, `nameSpaceIds`). Check 34
  recomputes both numbers and fails on any prose that disagrees.

Revision 12 answered the eleventh audit, which rejected one omission class and
three misclassifications:

- **Five public bit-fields are enumerated.** The declarator parser took the
  last identifier of a declaration, which for `unsigned deleted : 1;` is the
  width, so `CKey::deleted` (`include/extern/accumulo_data.h:47`) and the four
  `CRange` inclusive/infinite flags (lines 85-88) had no rows. Widths are now
  stripped per declarator, each named bit-field is one row, and the row records
  that the width is part of the ABI layout. These five are flat-C-API fields
  that a caller reads and writes directly.
- **A function-pointer typedef is an alias, not a function.**
  `typedef jint (*registerNatives_t)(JNIEnv *, jclass);`
  (`include/jni/JVMLoader.h:91`) was recorded as a callable free function. It
  now carries an alias row that says it names a callback type and declares no
  callable of its own.
- **pybind11 macro invocations are not declarations.**
  `PYBIND11_DECLARE_HOLDER_TYPE(...)` and `PYBIND11_EMBEDDED_MODULE(...)`
  (`include/jni/PythonBindings.h:49,51`) were recorded as free functions. Macro
  invocations whose macro is defined outside the pinned tree are recorded and
  excluded with a rationale; macro definitions and macro-declared types such as
  `stop_async_iteration` keep their rows. The Python surface that
  `PYBIND11_EMBEDDED_MODULE` registers is the server-side iterator module
  tracked by [SB-SCAN-016](#sec-9), not a C++ declaration surface.
- **`static` namespace-scope variables are internal linkage.** All five of
  them — `ROOT_EXTENT`, `syncBarrier`, `ACCUMULO_COORDINATOR`,
  `MASTER_COORDINATOR`, and `CLUSTER_COORDINATOR` — were described as objects
  consumers link against. They are `static`, so each translation unit gets its
  own copy. Their rows now say so, and [SB-CONN-010](#sec-7) is corrected:
  Sharkbite's pool is shared per translation unit, not process-wide, which
  changes what the divergence actually is. (Revision 12 stated seven here
  because forward declarations and a using-declaration were still miscounted as
  variables; revision 13 removed them and revision 14 corrected this sentence.)

Revision 11 answered the tenth audit, which rejected three scanner defects that
both hid obligations and inflated the required total:

- **Twelve `friend operator<<` functions are enumerated.** `friend` was a skip
  word, so every stream-insertion operator defined inside a class body was
  invisible: `Key` (two), `KeyExtent`, `KeyValue` (two), `Range` (two), `RFile`
  (two), `SequentialRFile` (two), and `RangeDefinition`. Each is a
  namespace-scope obligation reached by argument-dependent lookup, and each row
  names the befriending class. `friend class X;` declarations produce no row,
  so friendship is never mistaken for a type declaration.
- **Sixteen out-of-class definitions are merged, not duplicated.** A qualified
  definition such as `bool Sink<T>::enqueue(...)` was parsed as a new free
  function, which both double-counted the member and lost its access. Each is
  now matched to its in-class declaration by owner and member name; the merge
  and the in-class access are recorded.
- **Protected and private members can no longer be required.** Every
  declaration carries its access label, 700 protected and 346 private members
  are excluded by rule with their access recorded, and three rows revision 10
  required — `TransportPool::createNewTransport`, `Sink::enqueue`, and
  `Sink::exceedQueue` — are gone from the required total because their
  declarations are protected.
- **Net effect: −6 rows** (+12 friend operators, −16 merged definitions, −2
  namespace records that were a `friend class` forward declaration and a
  `using namespace` directive).

Revision 10 answered the ninth audit, which accepted the enumeration but
rejected four release-gating defects:

- **Templated members no longer make a type look memberless.** `typename`-
  introduced declarations were being skipped as statements, so
  `interconnect::CopyKey::operator()`
  (`include/interconnect/scanrequest/ScanIdentifier.h:24`) vanished and its
  owner was recorded as memberless. Memberless types fall from 8 to 7 and every
  remaining one was re-checked against templated members.
- **Conversion operators are parsed.** The operator matcher required the
  operator token to abut its parameter list, so
  `AccumuloInfoBuilder::operator AccumuloInfo &&()`
  (`include/data/constructs/coordinator/AccumuloInfo.h:202`) and
  `TabletServerStatusBuilder::operator TabletServerStatus &&()`
  (`include/data/constructs/coordinator/TabletServerStatus.h:222`) were dropped.
  Member operators rise from 141 to 144, and both conversion operators carry a
  note that implicit convertibility is itself the contract.
- **No unevaluated expression is presented as a numeric ordinal.** The
  anonymous enum in `include/data/constructs/inputvalidation.h:36` initialises
  `value` from `sizeof(test<T>(0)) == sizeof(char)`, which cannot be evaluated
  without instantiation. Its row now states that explicitly and quotes the
  initialiser verbatim instead of implying a computed value. Every enum and
  constant was re-tested: this is the only template-dependent initialiser in
  the live surface, and `true`/`false` and brace aggregates are evaluated
  exactly rather than flagged.
- **Narrative counts are reconciled mechanically.** [§1](#sec-1) claimed 199
  live-API headers while [§19.1](#sec-19-1) totalled 205; both now derive from
  the same extraction, and the verifier fails if any narrative count disagrees
  with the inventory.

Revision 9 answered the eighth audit, which rejected revision 8 for omissions
caused by scanner state and by an unsound vendoring heuristic:

- **+146 rows net.** Whole public sets that revision 8 dropped are enumerated:
  all of `utils::StringUtils`, `writer::Sink`, `cclient::data::KeyAllocatorPool`,
  and the `Hdfs`/`HdfsInputStream`/`HdfsOutputStream` wrappers, the four
  templated `StringUtils::join` overloads that a non-balanced template-prefix
  strip had discarded, plus 108
  namespace-scope functions (was 78), namespace-scope variables (was 0), and
  the `LOG_LEVEL` enum.
- **Vendoring is decided by path and by the file's own license**, never by a
  reference the file makes; the exclusion set is 152 headers, itemised in
  [§19.1](#sec-19-1).
- **Nine include-guard artifacts are gone**, including the `#define NAME 1`
  spelling that revision 8's guard test missed.
- **Five new class-coverage checks** ([§19.3](#sec-19-3)) compare the inventory
  against the headers rather than the document against itself, which is the
  only way this class of omission is detectable.
- **No new `Covered` rows.** Nothing in this revision adds evidence, so the
  count stays at zero, as required.

Counts are mechanically derived from this file: each matrix row is a table line
whose first cell begins with `SB-` and that contains exactly one of the six
status strings in its own cell. Re-run that extraction after any edit and update
this section.

## 26. Divergences requiring explicit approval

Twelve entries below are approved: [SB-DIV-001](#sec-26) through
[SB-DIV-005](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-007](#sec-26) through [SB-DIV-009](#sec-26),
[SB-DIV-016](#sec-26) through [SB-DIV-019](#sec-26),
signed by @phrocker on **2026-08-20** or the earlier
date shown in the table. [SB-DIV-013](#sec-26) is **subsumed** by [SB-DIV-016](#sec-26):
it is dormant rather than blocking, carries no approver of its own, and revives
only if that approval is reversed. Every remaining entry blocks the gate until a
named approver signs it with a date. Approvals are recorded on Shoal issue
[#81](https://github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/issues/81) and then mirrored into
this table in the same change; a comment on #81 alone does not lift the gate,
and neither does an edit here without the corresponding #81 decision. Adding a
divergence to this table is not approval.

**98 matrix rows currently carry the `Intentional divergence (approval
required)` status: 98 are approved and 0 are not.** The approved 82 are the
cluster-status rows of [§14](#sec-14), all covered by the single decision
[SB-DIV-016](#sec-26), which @phrocker approved on **2026-08-19**; that decision
also governs [SB-CONN-007](#sec-7), the `getStatistics()` entry point, but does
not cover it as an approved row, so it stays `Missing Go` and is counted there.
The additional approved rows are SB-PKG-001 (independent distribution/version), SB-PKG-007 (Python 3.9+), SB-PKG-014 (Accumulo 4 only), SB-CFG-014 and
SB-CFG-022 (no password read-back, both spellings), SB-CONN-010
(per-connector pools), SB-ERR-003 (no Thrift types),
SB-SCAN-007/016 (stable rejection of non-functional Python iterators), and
SB-SCAN-008/009/014/015 (no implicit hedged or RFile-only scans),
SB-WRITE-010 (structured write failures rather than silent discard), plus SB-TABLE-006 (no compatible
online-compaction contract) and SB-TABLE-013 (no compatible legacy bulk-import
contract).
The table below lists 19 decisions — 12 approved, 1 subsumed by that approval,
and 6 still proposed — because one decision can cover many rows; the row count
and the decision count are different quantities and must not be conflated.

The remaining 6 entries — every decision except the approved [SB-DIV-001](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-002](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-003](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-004](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-005](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-007](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-008](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-009](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-016](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-017](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-018](#sec-26), [SB-DIV-019](#sec-26) and the subsumed [SB-DIV-013](#sec-26) — are **proposed** divergences. Every row named by those proposals currently carries a non-divergence gap status; approval would move it to `Intentional divergence`. Rejecting a
proposal leaves its rows as gaps that must be implemented. Neither of the two
non-proposed entries is a proposal: SB-DIV-016 is already approved, and
SB-DIV-013 describes a capability that same approval removed outright, so it has
nothing left to propose. SB-DIV-016 names [SB-CONN-007](#sec-7) as the entry
point that reaches its rows, but that row is outside the approved set and is `Covered` because the required raising shim has landed; only the 82 unavailable capability rows retain divergence status. An
approved divergence never becomes `Covered`: it records a capability that will
never exist rather than one that has been delivered, and its rows keep the
`approval required` label because [§4.2](#sec-4) fixes the six status names —
approval state lives in this table, not in the status column.
